traits.fan_split_depth.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 281): the blade divided a quarter to a third of the way to its base into single-fold pointed segments.

traits.segment_posture.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 281): the segments thick and very stiff.

traits.segment_filaments.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 281) names no threads; the segments' margins are often spiny instead (not drawn).

traits.petiole_armature.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 281): an armed palm, the petiole's margins armed with stout teeth; drawn at the family's size and spacing for stout teeth, as no size is given.

traits.petiole_tooth_form.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 281): stout teeth, no curve named; drawn square to the petiole.

traits.petiole_teeth_distal.note: Dransfield et al. (2008, p. 281) names no change in the teeth toward the blade; drawn even.

traits.leaf_division.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.leaf_incision.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. A fan palm's blade is one piece cut into segments: simple, parted, palmate.

traits.division_pattern.note: Mabberley's Plant-book (4th ed., 2017), under Palmae, subfamily III Coryphoideae: leaves induplicately palmate in all but Phoenix and the Caryoteae (Arenga, Caryota, Wallichia), which are pinnate. generator.params.costa.why: The rib the fan's segments rise from, as a share of the frond: a fifth for a strongly costapalmate fan, a tenth for a shortly costapalmate one (the built-in cabbage and California fan palms, 0.18 and 0.12).

rules.note: Dransfield et al. (Genera Palmarum, 2nd ed., 2008), under the genus: its fan leaves are shortly costapalmate, the rib running only a little into the blade.
